title: Safeguards to Prevent Entry into Singapore by Individuals Using Fraudulent Documents or Data
what_it_is: Safeguards to Prevent Entry into Singapore by Individuals Using Fraudulent Documents or Data

sections.label: ICA entry risk safeguards
sections.summary: Questions ask how ICA mitigates fraudulent document entry, what safeguards beyond biometrics exist, and what steps ICA will take.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in view of the undetected entry of an extremist preacher on 9 August 2024 (a) how does the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) mitigate the risk of individuals using fraudulent documents to enter Singapore, especially with increased automation at immigration checkpoints; (b) beyond the use of biometrics, what other safeguards, such as equipping frontline personnel with lists of individuals of concern, are in place to identify dangerous individuals; and (c) what concrete steps will ICA take to enhance the detection of such individuals.

sections.label: Bangladeshi preacher dormitory questions
sections.summary: Questions ask for updates on the Bangladeshi preacher investigation, detentions, his entry and preaching history, and dormitory owner compliance and penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update on the investigation into the case of a Bangladeshi preacher giving illegal sermons at a dormitory in Tuas; (b) whether any person has been detained in relation to the said incident; and (c) how many times has the Bangladeshi preacher entered Singapore in the last 10 years and how many times has he preached in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Ministry will be taking steps to ensure that dormitory owners comply with all rules and regulations before permitting foreign speakers from conducting talks or programmes to migrant workers residing in their dormitories; (b) to date, how many cases of foreign visitors who have conducted an event without valid permits have been detected in foreign worker dormitories; and (c) what are some of the penalties in place to deal with the dormitory owners when such incidents occur.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant
sentences.text: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam): Sir, with your permission, can I take together the questions relating to the case of the foreign preacher, Amir Hamza?

sections.label: Amir Hamza unlawful preaching
sections.summary: Amir Hamza was invited by a dormitory operator, entered Singapore on 9 August 2024, and preached without a permit, which was unlawful.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Amir Hamza was invited by a dormitory operator.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He came into Singapore on Independence Day, 9 August 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He preached to a group to Bangladeshi migrant workers on the same day at a dormitory.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And he did so without a permit – that was unlawful.

sections.label: Fraudulent passport detections
sections.summary: Since 2022, about 30 visitors monthly with legitimate passports but different identities from ICA records were detected and refused entry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Since 2022, every month, about 30 visitors with legitimate passports but containing a different identity from ICA’s records were detected and refused entry.

sections.label: Foreign speaker permit offences
sections.summary: Foreigners speaking at religious, cause-based or political events need a Miscellaneous Work Pass; the dormitory operator is investigated for several offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Third, foreigners who wish to speak at public events that are religious, cause-based or political in nature are required to obtain a Miscellaneous Work Pass under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The offences that are being looked into include participation in an unlawful assembly under the Public Order Act and not obtaining a Miscellaneous Work Permit required under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The dormitory operator was also the event organiser.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He is being investigated for several offences including those under the Public Order Act, Employment of Foreign Manpower Act and Foreign Employee Dormitories Act.

sections.label: Visa sponsor agent case
sections.summary: There was a visa and a sponsor but no agent because the sponsor is related to the dormitory operator, who is also being investigated.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: To the second question, yes, there would normally be a visa.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There would have to be a sponsor and there will have to be an agent.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But in this case, there was a visa, there was a sponsor, but there is no agent because the person who sponsored is related to the dormitory operator and that person is being investigated as well.

sections.label: Comprehensive data on excluded persons
sections.summary: No country has such a comprehensive set of data on all potential persons who might have to be excluded.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As I said, no country in the world has such a comprehensive set of data on all potential persons who might have to be excluded.
